entries.gave: Read the Cut, invoicer as round 1 left it (command.py, lines.py, render.py, tax.py, totals.py, tests, pyproject.toml), round 1 made.json and try.jsonl, and the three Mores kept. People: accounting colleagues who save an invoice's lines from a spreadsheet and run `invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT` to print it at the client's rate, with no Python; and the developer who pipx-installs it once. They achieve an invoice correct enough to send a client: every amount to the cent, credit lines allowed, and every wrong input refused with one actionable line.
Read code best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-code best-practice.md, to their end, before any change.

Unit cases opened from the Cut (no architecture): existing 23 tests plus new cases: each amount to the cent (89.5, 100, 12.345x3), subtotal as the sum of the printed amounts, credit lines (negative price, negative quantity, quantity 0), refusals of a folder, an unreadable file, a price/quantity/amount out of -1e9..1e9 (1e400), a row of four fields, a rate between 0 and 1 without %; edges: rate 1 taken, 0.5% taken, 999999999.99 taken, 1000000000 refused.

Left to the code: how a line amount is rounded (half up to the cent, as tax_of already rounds), whether the subtotal sums the rounded or the unrounded amounts (the rounded, so the printed lines add up), the limit on a number (below 1000000000 either side of zero), and how a rate below 1 is told from a percent (refused unless written with %).

Each decision to one module: rounding to the cent in tax.py (to_cent, used by tax_of and render), the invoice text in render.py, reading rows and their limits in lines.py, the command line, the file and the rate in command.py. No new module.
No variant that the cases call for, so no pattern.
Offered: tax.to_cent (render and tax_of call it), alongside the names already offered; the limit and quantity pattern stay internal in lines.py.

Each planned branch named by its case: to_cent by the cent cases; the limit by the 1e400 and edge cases; the minus in the quantity by the credit case; IsADirectoryError and PermissionError by the folder and unreadable cases; the fraction refusal by --rate 0.19 and its % edge. No option or parameter added.

No module added; supporting cases in test_lines.py for parse_lines (negative price, negative quantity, quantity 0, four fields, price/quantity/amount limits and their edges) support test_command cases test_prints_a_credit_line and test_refuses_a_price_too_large_to_print.
No case found that supports no unit case of the part; nothing to ask.
Inputs from outside: argv (LINES, --rate) in command.main via argparse and _rate; the file at LINES where main opens it; its text in lines.parse_lines, each row read in _line, _price, _quantity.
Test command from pyproject.toml head comment: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.
The manifest gives the command, so no search for a runner needed.
Ran the tests in a throwaway copy before any change: 23 run, OK.
Things and names: a line (Line, line), a row of text (row), its amount (amount(), and in render amount for the subtotal), the tax rate (rate, percent), the file of lines (LINES, path, saved).
No architecture or README text for these; the Cut says line, row, price, quantity, tax rate, subtotal, total.
No two names for one thing to merge beyond those the Cut uses.
One name for two things: amount in render named the subtotal while Line.amount names a line amount; render names it subtotal_amount... renamed to subtotal in render, as the Cut names it.

Rules written in more than one place: rounding to the cent half up (tax.py; now also needed by render), the row form ROW (lines.py, used by command), the limit on a number (new, lines.py only), the column formats of render (left as the round records keep that More).
Rounding of a line amount and of the tax would change together, as an invoice rounds every amount one way, so they are one rule.
Rounding kept by tax.py, which already holds CENT and ROUND_HALF_UP and which render already imports; render calls to_cent from it.

Kinds: refusing a row (LineError naming the row), refusing an argument (argparse.ArgumentTypeError), refusing the file (parser.error), rounding to the cent, tests of the command (run_command helper) and of parse_lines (assertRaises with the whole message).
Each kind is done one way now; the new refusals of a folder and an unreadable file go through parser.error like the missing file, and the limits through LineError like the other row refusals.
No style settings (no ruff config); took the way the code uses most, as listed.
No new way chosen.

Decided: every Cut decision taken as it stands. Settled by purpose: line amounts rounded half up to the cent by tax.to_cent, the subtotal the sum of the rounded amounts, the total subtotal plus tax; a price, a quantity and a line amount each between -1000000000 and 1000000000, else refused naming the row; quantity a whole number with an optional minus, 0 allowed; a folder or unreadable file refused by parser.error; a rate above 0 and below 1 refused unless written with %. Nothing left open, so no asks.

Searched tests for render, parse_lines, _rate and main: render reached only through main (whole output asserted at two decimals); parse_lines refusals all pinned; nothing pins tax.CENT or totals beyond render.

Ran the 20 new or changed tests before the code: 15 fail, each for its Then (89.5 printed, 0.015 subtotal, credit rows refused, no refusal of 1e400, 0.19 or the limits, traceback on a folder and an unreadable file); the four edge tests that pass today (rate 1, 0.5%, 999999999.99, 499999999.99x2) pin behavior kept.

tax.py opening now reads How an amount, and the tax of an amount, are rounded to the cent; the other modules openings still state their one decision (render: the invoice as text; lines: which rows give a line; command: what the command takes and prints).

Tried changes from openings alone: round to whole euros -> tax.py; a credit line in a separate column -> render.py; a larger limit on a price -> lines.py; a new option such as --currency -> command.py. Each names one module.
New offered name tax.to_cent written untyped like tax_of beside it, as the type hints of the older modules are a More left in the round records; lines.py and command.py keep their types.

Doc comments updated: to_cent (half up, examples), render (amounts to the cent, subtotal of amounts as shown), parse_lines (negative price, quantity 0 or negative, limits, refusals), main (rate below 1 needs %, folder, permission), _rate.

Checked each test value against the doc comments: rounding half up, the subtotal of amounts as shown, -1 and 0 quantities, the exact limits, 0.5% taken and 0.19 refused, folder and permission refusals are each stated.

Wrote the least code under each failing test: to_cent and its use in render for the cent tests, the minus and the 9-digit bound in _WHOLE for the credit and quantity tests, the _LIMIT checks for price and amount, two except clauses, one fraction check in _rate.
Ran the tests after the code: 43 run, OK.
Read each body: the quantity no longer needs an int() < 1 check, removed; no option, mode or fallback without a case.
pyproject.toml unchanged: Python 3.9 or later, no dependency, the pipx install and the test command in its head; no new dependency added.
The new command tests make their file or use their own temporary folder (folder case, chmod 0 case) from setUp, removed by addCleanup.
The tests run no real tool beyond Python; the permission test skips under root, who reads any file.
Ran the tests shuffled with seeds 7, 314 and 2026: 43 run, 0 failed, 0 skipped each.
In a throwaway copy with an empty home, the setup alone (pip install of the repository) gives bin/invoicer, which prints the invoice; the tests run there by the manifest command, 43 OK.

One test per case: 8 in test_command (cents, subtotal as printed, credit line, rate 1, rate 0.19 refused, 0.5% taken, folder, unreadable, four fields, 1e400) and 12 in test_lines (four fields, price limit and edges, negative price, negative quantity, quantity 0, quantity limit and edge, amount limit and edge); no name needs and.

Expected values worked out from each Then by hand before running: 37.035 to 37.04, 226.54 x 0.19 = 43.0426 to 43.04, 169.50 x 0.19 = 32.205 to 32.21, 210.50 x 0.01 = 2.105 to 2.11, x 0.005 = 1.0525 to 1.05.
Each test holds its rows and expected rows in its own body; only saved, run_command and row are shared setup.
No loop or branch in any test; the root skip is a decorator, not a branch in the body.
Failure messages added where name and values do not say it: the refused price/quantity is named, 210.50 at 1% is 2.105, at 0.5% is 1.0525.
Real modules and real temporary files in every test; no test double.
Tests call only main and parse_lines and read Line fields that Line offers; none reaches _LIMIT, _WHOLE, _rate or _price.
Changed bodies without changing interfaces (rewrote tax_of over to_cent, replaced the int() < 1 check by the pattern, render no longer calls totals.subtotal): tests still pass, none rewritten.
The cent, subtotal and credit tests assert the whole printed text or the last rows in full; the refusals assert code, empty output and the whole message.
coverage.py with branches: command 100%, lines 98% (34, Line.__repr__), render 100%, tax 100%, totals 57% (10, 15-16).

Uncovered: Line.__repr__ and totals.subtotal/total, which render no longer calls; all are names the package offers in __all__ to callers outside, and total() unused and the older modules are Mores left in the round records, so kept and not removed; no case of the command calls for them.
No Test strategy names an interface for property-based tests; none written.
No property-based test ran, so no failing input to weigh.
The round takes no CI mutation report (the repository CI runs lint only); no mutant listed.
No mutant listed, nothing to remove.
No mutant listed, nothing to mark.
No mutant listed; the >= at each limit is pinned by the at-the-limit and just-below tests on both sides.

Each input read where it enters: the rate in _rate (range, fraction), the file at open (missing, folder, permission, encoding), each row in _line/_price/_quantity (fields, number, whole, limits) before render runs.
A rate above 0 and below 1 without % can be read two ways (a fraction or a percent), so it is refused, not guessed; with % it reads one way and is taken.
Caught by own type only IsADirectoryError and PermissionError, beside FileNotFoundError, UnicodeDecodeError and LineError, each with what to fix; any other OSError keeps its trace.

Each new message names invoicer, the file and row or --rate, what was wrong, and what is taken, such as invoicer: error: big.csv, row 1: the price must be between -1000000000 and 1000000000, not 1e400.
Every new check is an if that raises; no assert.
Ran the installed invoicer on 1e400, four fields, chmod 0 file, a folder, --rate 0.19: each refused with exit 2 and one line from which the input can be fixed without the code.

Behaviors kept that no test reached before: tax_of rounding half up is pinned through the command (39.995 to 40.00, 32.205 to 32.21); a price of 999999999.99 and an amount of 999999999.98 pinned as taken.
Structure steps taken one at a time with the tests run between: extract to_cent from tax_of; have render call to_cent; drop render import of totals.subtotal.
No name that a test uses was renamed; the changed expectations (quantity message, quantity 0 now read) are behavior the Cut decisions N3 credit lines change, not a rename.
Tests run after each step: 43 OK; no step undone.

The behavior that looked wrong, refusing negative prices and quantities, came back to the callers by the Cut decision on credit lines; totals.subtotal still sums unrounded amounts as its doc says, which no caller in the repository now uses, so nothing to ask.
Searched each name: CENT used by to_cent, _BETWEEN by three messages, _LIMIT by the checks; subtotal and total are named in __init__ __all__, the package interface, so kept.
tax_of now only passes amount * rate to to_cent, but it adds the multiplication and is offered by the package, so kept.
No new parameter; render currency left as the round records keep that More.
Comments read against code: the _WHOLE and _LIMIT comments say what the code cannot (why 9 digits, why the limit); the utf-8-sig comment stays.

Read new names where used: to_cent rounds to the cent; _LIMIT the size a number stays below; _BETWEEN the range as messages say it; written_as_percent whether the rate ends in %; amounts the line amounts as printed; subtotal in render the subtotal printed.
Each definition matches the words; render amount for the subtotal renamed subtotal; no other rename.
Renamed render local amount (the subtotal) to subtotal, the one rename, with tests run.

One sentence each: to_cent rounds an amount half up to the cent; render lays out each line amount, the subtotal, tax and total to the cent; _line reads a row into a Line within the limit; _price reads a price within the limit; _quantity reads a whole quantity; _rate reads the percent into a fraction; each new test checks one case.
No line stopped the reading; the render comprehension over zip stays one plain step.
No sentence joins two tasks a caller wants apart; _line reads the fields and checks the amount of the line it builds, one task.
Functions read _LIMIT and _BETWEEN, module constants named and commented at the top of the module, as _WHOLE and ROW already are; no hidden global setting.
No function mixes two levels.
No new single-caller function without a name of its own; to_cent has two callers.
Marked as looking odd: the 9-digit bound in _WHOLE, the limit of a billion, render summing rounded amounts instead of calling subtotal(), the fraction refusal of a rate below 1.
Named where a name says it: _LIMIT, _BETWEEN, written_as_percent.

Wrote the reasons in place: _WHOLE comment (9 digits keep it below _LIMIT), _LIMIT comment (a mistyped cell, sums exact to the cent), render docstring (subtotal adds the amounts as shown), _rate docstring (below 1 needs %).
Every mark had a reason from the Cut; nothing left to ask.
Corrected comments that no longer held: parse_lines, _quantity and main docstrings no longer say a quantity from 1 or omit the new refusals; tax.py opening says it rounds amounts too.
Rounding to the cent written once in tax.to_cent, used by tax_of and render; the limit once in lines._LIMIT, its words once in _BETWEEN.
No shared function with a flag picking a branch.
No code uses another module underscore name; render uses to_cent, which tax offers.
Every place reads one Python definition; no cross-language copy.
New refusals written the chosen ways: rows by LineError naming the row, the file by parser.error, the rate by ArgumentTypeError; new tests in the existing assertRaises and run_command forms.
No place keeps a different way.

Made: tax.to_cent and tax_of over it; render prints each amount, the subtotal of the amounts as printed, the tax and the total to the cent; lines.parse_lines reads negative prices and quantities of 0 or below, refuses a price, quantity or amount not between -1000000000 and 1000000000; command refuses a folder, a file without read permission, and a rate above 0 and below 1 written without %. 20 tests added or changed; 43 pass.

Tried in throwaway copies as accounting would, after pip install of the repository: a CSV UTF-8 file with CRLF and BOM, prices 89.5, 100, 12.345 and a credit of -25 at --rate 19 prints every amount to the cent and a total of subtotal plus tax (exit 0); --rate 0.07, a folder, 1e400, four fields, a chmod 0 file and a quantity of 11 digits each refused with one line and exit 2. 43 tests OK, three shuffled runs OK, coverage 97%.

Wrote the Made at rounds/invoicer/2/made.json: where each of the six Cut decisions and the three Mores kept land, and six points settled with their grounds (cent rounding half up, subtotal of printed amounts, the billion limit, 0.5% taken, the permission message, a quantity of 0).
Ending with done: the Made is written and rn check reads the record and the Made.
